speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Good evening. Hope everyone’s well. As always,  great questions. Hello. Can you tell us about  
the players that have hurt? How badly are they  injured? I’m really happy for the win. We talked  
about game one and how important that was. We said  on the job we should have finished probably with  
a bigger margin in certain moments of the game,  but when it’s 1-0 it’s always tough because they  
have quality, because they brought so many good  players from the bench as well. And when we don’t  
finish the action, especially the open ones that  we had, the margins are going to be smaller. But  
in relation to the two players that you mentioned,  they are still muscular niggles. We don’t think  
it’s too much. We have to wait and see if  they’re going to be available for Wednesday.  
James from CBS. Do you feel like you could take  four games as emotionally draining as that? Yes,  
we’re taking 50. How many we play now, and we are  where we are. I don’t expect after 22 years not  
winning it that it’s going to be a path of roses  and beautiful music around it. So it’s going to be  
like this and we are ready for it. Tom, there  seems to be such a swell around the idea of having  
to score loads of goals. We have the table leads.  You said on Friday that every game in the Premier  
League is so hard. Was that the best example of  it? It is. It’s so hard to win in this league.  
We know that. That’s why the amount of points that  the team that we have now compared to other years  
is different. And the reason is because it’s so  competitive, so difficult to do it. And we know  
at half-time the message was clear, we need to go  score the second goal. We tried, but when you are  
not that efficient in certain areas, we certainly  have to have other things to win the game. How  
important was it to see Bukayo back on the pitch  smiling? Great. And I think he had some very good  
impact as well in the minutes that he’s played. So  he’s back. I think he looks sharp. He looked good,  
he looked fresh. You certainly notice something  different in the team, in the stadium as well,  
when he comes in. So we certainly need that.  So do you think he’s now fine as far as you’re  
concerned going forward? Are you still having to  take it easy? Let’s see how he reacts tomorrow,  
how he absorbs the load. But yeah, he’s so keen,  he’s so motivated. It’s the most beautiful part of  
the season and he’s with us. Alex Bibersey. Hi.  Is there a bigger meaning in this win as well,  
being able to put the pressure back on to  Manchester City? Are you proud of how you  
managed it? We had to do what was in our hands and  we discussed that. That’s a game. One is in our  
hands, what we do, how we approach the game. Are  we able to win it? We’ve done it. We wanted bigger  
margins. It’s not impossible, but we certainly  done the job. Phil. Just on those emotions,  
Mikel, you spoke about earlier, what is it  like when you’re on the touchline watching it,  
with every kick matters and every point obviously  now matters? Just try to play the game with the  
boys because I know the immense effort that they  are putting in. I know how much they want it and  
when certain actions don’t go your way, and  I see the way they react and they know it and  
they just try back and they are so willing. Just  be close to them, try to pass my energy on and  
help them. You got three points, which is the  most important thing, but when it’s so tight at  
the end, in the last couple of minutes, not  tight, but when there are the nerves in it,  
just one fluky action can lead to a goal. Is  that kind of saying that these next four games,  
you need that extra goal just to dampen it? Yeah.  And you had two or three much better, especially  
we had some open situations to score the goal,  very clear. I have to say as well, in my opinion,  
it’s a clear red card. I watched it 10 times.  If you have ever played football, it is a red  
card. It’s the second time in two games, because  against Manchester City, when Kai Havertz goes  
through and the goalkeeper is falling one v one,  the title is there. It is a red card, guys. So  
these are the margins as well and hopefully  that’s going to change. Why do you not get  
a red? I don’t know. I don’t know. So they will  have their opinion. I’m here to give my opinion.  
And somebody that has been in the game for a  long time, and you talk to any of the players,  
because the trajectory where the ball is, there’s  no keeper there. If that were happening the other  
way around, it’s a red card. Dave. I was going to  ask something else, but just on the possible red,  
do you feel that things are going more against  you than for you in terms of those decisions?  
I’m saying the reality of the last two games  in crucial moments when everything at stake is,  
we need everything to go our way. And it hasn’t.  I’m not putting any excuses. I’m the first one to  
understand. I didn’t talk about it when we lost  the game. I’m doing it when we won. It’s a red  
card. Today is a red card. In Manchester and the  world is different. That’s it. Can I just quickly  
ask you about the short corners? Sorry, Dan.  We’ve talked a lot about corners all season.  
You’ve obviously done a lot of damage with your  corners, but you went, it felt like, you found a  
different way today. You have to add everything  that we do in the game. When the teams adapt to  
certain things, with teams that are so physical  that they can defend naturally, you have to find  
other ways. The thing that I love best is the  courage of the players because we played short,  
and you could see the reaction of the crowd  because we went with the direction. And the second  
one, we did it again and Ebs shoots with the left  foot and puts it out. And the third one we are,  
and we score. And to have this, I was going to say  another word, courage, big courage, in this moment  
when the pressure is on, when the reaction is like  this, to play, that is exactly what I want for the  
team because the player has to make the decision  that he believes is the best. Charlie. You  
mentioned Eze there. How pleased are you that he  scored another great goal in front of the England  
manager as well? He could have a really big  summer, couldn’t he? And you mentioned it earlier.  
Hopefully it’s not too serious. Was he a bit  disappointed though that he had to come off? For  
sure. Obviously he’s a big player for us and he’s  in a really good moment. He produced an incredible  
moment to score the goal and, as I said, hopefully  he’s fit and he can be with us on Wednesday. OK,  
last couple. Hi. I think Kai Havertz has played so  well recently and today again until he came off.  
Can you just clarify what’s the issue with him and  have you spoken to him yet? No, I haven’t, but he  
had a little niggle, so I don’t know how serious  it is. It didn’t look too big because the action,  
the way he describes it, is not too sharp, but we  have to wait and see. Thank you. Zubi was sick at  
half-time, wasn’t feeling good, and he tried his  very best. I think he played a really good game.  
The idea, we had to take him off. Just wanted to  ask, Nørgaard’s not played as much throughout the  
season because this guy has been exceptional.  I understand that, but today I had to leave  
two players out of the squad. At the end, Mikel is  out, and they were Cristhian and Ricky. So that’s  
going to happen. As I said, if the Premier League  allows us to have 20 or 22 players, we can have  
everybody. Everybody feels involved, and hopefully  next season that will be the case. Thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Arsenal 1-0 Newcastle United | Premier League
